A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BiDoRA, with matching algorithms, equations, and original experiments. The main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning results on GLUE, Reuters21578, E2E, BioNLP, and CoNLL2003, together with ablations, training curves, and weight-decomposition analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds biomedical evaluations, DeBERTa-XXL experiments, broader baseline comparisons, and supplementary analyses. Some comparison scores are explicitly sourced from cited work, but BiDoRA's original results are clearly reported.

M1.justification: The weight decomposition, orthogonal regularizer, bi-level objectives, approximate hypergradient updates, and direction-retraining procedure remain unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithm 1. Retraining magnitude is introduced as an ablation, not as a replacement method.

E1.justification: v2 adds protein thermostability classification, blood-brain barrier peptide classification, and minimum inhibitory concentration regression using ESM (Section 5.3 and Appendix A.4). These substantially extend coverage beyond v1's language tasks, including its biomedical named-entity recognition task. Original datasets remain represented, with several evaluations moved to Appendix H.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's FT, Adapter, LoRA, and DoRA comparisons, v2 Table 2 includes BitFit, AdaLoRA, AFLoRA, LaMDA, VeRA, FourierFT, SSH, and MaCP in the reported GLUE comparison. Section 5.2 explicitly identifies published baseline scores taken from Shen et al.; these are actual comparison entries, not merely additional citations.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce DeBERTa-XXL and ESM configurations, plus a separate GLUE comparison at ranks 8 and 16 with different bias handling (Table 2 and Appendix B). Training-gap analysis adds a moving-average metric with decay 0.99 and weighted inner/outer-loop aggregation. Cost evaluation expands from three named GLUE tasks to the GLUE benchmark with convergence-step and total-time measurements. Original RoBERTa and GPT-2 hyperparameter tables are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds rank sensitivity, quantitative training/test gaps, magnitude-versus-direction retraining, DoRA weight-decay/dropout controls, and eigenspectrum analysis of orthogonal regularization (Tables 2, 3, 5, 11 and Figure 5). Conversely, v1 Figure 4's CoLA/SST-2 training/validation/test analysis is removed. Existing partition-ratio sensitivity and query/value weight-decomposition analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 adds a Wilcoxon signed-rank test reporting p = 2.4e-4 (Section 5.6). It uses 27 paired entries: eight task scores plus their average for each of three models. This is a new statistical analysis, although including averages alongside their component scores introduces dependence. No repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals are added.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for new models, biomedical tasks, expanded comparisons, and ablations. Existing results also change: LoRA's E2E BLEU/NIST/METEOR/CIDEr values move from 63.7/8.19/44.1/2.17 in v1 Table 3 to 67.1/8.54/45.7/2.33 in v2 Table 12, without a documented corresponding setting change. Original RoBERTa GLUE, Reuters, and token-classification scores remain. The new cost breakdown replaces the earlier three-task summary; its different scope prevents interpreting the lower normalized total time as a same-setting speedup.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix D explicitly applies a cited generalization theorem's validation-size versus effective-hyperparameter condition to BiDoRA; v2 removes this argument. The bi-level objectives, hypergradient derivation, and weight-decomposition definitions remain mathematically equivalent. New references to convergence and generalization research do not introduce a new proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions—bi-level magnitude/direction optimization, reduced overfitting, and updates resembling full fine-tuning—remain unchanged. v2's abstract broadens the performance claim to extremely small biomedical datasets and more leading PEFT methods, and explicitly claims statistical significance using the new test.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of rank robustness, conventional regularization controls, and orthogonality evidence. It replaces v1's specific generalization-guarantee discussion with broader theoretical motivation and explicitly acknowledges the absence of formal analysis of improved decoupling. Training efficiency becomes an explicit limitation, while Appendix E argues that fewer convergence steps moderate the per-step overhead. These materially revise the explanation and qualification of the method's benefits.

D1.justification: v2 adds stopping criteria, bias-handling information, the ESM Protein Aligner checkpoint, and a named GitHub code link replacing the anonymous repository link. Original hyperparameter values are preserved, but v1's explicit query/value adaptation instruction is removed. Biomedical sample-count disclosures conflict: Section 5.3 and Appendix A.4 assign 936/3,695 training samples to thermostability/MIC, while Table 6 reverses them. The stopping description newly mentions monitoring test performance; it does not establish a changed procedure.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands coverage of recent PEFT approaches, including SAN, FADA, SET, VeRA, AFLoRA, and spectral adaptation methods. v2 also adds biomedical, convergence, and prospective hypergradient-estimator references, while removing much of the literature supporting v1 Appendix D. Research positioning shifts toward broader empirical comparison and qualified theoretical motivation.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, method explanations are expanded, and the experimental narrative is reorganized around GLUE and small biomedical datasets. Generation, token classification, Reuters results, and computational costs move into appendices. A new discussion and expanded conclusion replace the earlier structure, alongside terminology, affiliation, and publication-header edits.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with clearer component states and optimization labels. Existing plots are relocated, the validation/test plot is removed, and a six-panel eigenspectrum figure is added. Dataset summaries and hyperparameter tables are consolidated, Reuters and token-classification results are merged, and several new comparison tables appear. Table sizing, typography, and page layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: The broader comparisons and targeted rank, retraining, and regularization controls better test the central performance and overfitting claims. Explicit limitations and clearer cost accounting also improve the paper. These benefits are tempered by the dependent entries in the new significance test, conflicting biomedical sample counts, and newly disclosed test-based stopping, which raises evaluation concerns without establishing a change from v1. The revision provides useful additional evidence and clarity, but the reporting weaknesses limit the overall quality gain.
